To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) ImageNet accuracy is a strong predictor of performance on downstream tasks, (b) the best models on ImageNet transfer to a variety of downstream tasks better than models trained on those tasks, (c) ImageNet accuracy does not predict transfer performance for models trained on a subset of the ImageNet classes, and (d) the best models for transfer are trained on the full ImageNet dataset.

1. The best-performing ImageNet model (ResNet152) has the best transfer performance to the PASCAL VOC 2007 and 2012 detection datasets, and 2. The best-performed model on the ImageNet classification task (Inception-v4) has the best performance on the ImageNet localization task.
Better ImageNet models are not necessarily more effective at transfer learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question: "Does a model trained on ImageNet perform better than a model trained on a different task on a given test set?" We are not concerned with the question "Does a model perform well on a given task?

the question of whether one architecture is more likely than another to perform well on a given task, and we do not attempt to quantify the variability of the performance of a given architecture on a given dataset.
whether the ImageNet models are better than previous models on a variety of tasks, and whether the ImageNet model is better than the VGG model on the ImageNet task.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ImageNet-trained models perform better on ImageNet than the models trained on ImageNet and VOC2007, and that the ImageNet models perform better than the models trained with VOC2007 alone.
, in our experiments, the best ImageNet models transfer well to other datasets, and the best performing ImageNet models transfer better than others.

the ResNet models are significantly better than the AlexNet models on the test set distribution, but we do not have evidence that this difference is significant in terms of generalization to new data drawn from a different distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a given model, the ImageNet accuracy of the model is a good predictor of the model's performance on a variety of downstream tasks, but the ImageNet accuracy is not a perfect predictor of the model performance.
we have not observed a consistent pattern of better performance of one architecture over another on the test sets of the datasets we have examined.
the ImageNet models trained with the ResNet architecture are superior on the ImageNet dataset, and the VGG16 architecture is superior on the PASCAL VOC 2007 dataset.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ImageNet models trained with the ResNet-50 architecture are superior on the test set, and we believe that the superiority of these models on the test set is likely to transfer to other datasets.
ImageNet models trained with the same architecture and data can vary substantially in their performance on downstream tasks.
, on ImageNet, the difference in accuracy across architectures is much larger than the difference in accuracy due to training a network from a different random initialization or training order.
